overview: This table sets the objectives the player sees in battle, including what to do and how much, and shapes Binding Vow choices between fights.
description: Parallel-array mission objectives: each indexed slot pairs a battle-log value, target, passive classification and comparison threshold, producing per-index progress for the battle HUD and PvE completion counters; story objectives/rewards read the same rows by a shifted index, and the row can also ban binding-vow effects.

Id.simple: The name the game uses to pick this task for a stage or story battle.
Id.technical: FName import key / DataTable row name (export property `ID`); no runtime consumer reads the row's Id member as data. GameDataTableManager loads the named MissionTaskDataTable into `MissionTaskDataTables` (DTM+0x9E0). Arcade, story and PvE wave setup resolve the id from `MissionWave.Id_MissionTaskLottery` through `BattleArcade_PickLotteryTask` (weighted, None candidates dropped), and PvE caches the picked ids in `FGamePvESettings::MissionTaskIds`. The story-demo helper instead takes `MissionTaskLottery.Id_MissionTask[0]` without using its weight.

ValueType.simple: What the fight measures for each objective, such as hits, Cursed Energy, health, or who attacks first.
ValueType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogValueType>, default empty. `ValueType.Num()` is the authoritative condition count in `Tick`, `FailFirstAttackTasks` and `OnEvent13`; all exported rows have three slots and the third is always `None`. Slot i is passed with `TargetType[i]` and `PassiveType[i]` to `AGameBattleManager::EvaluateLog` (GM 0x1015A80 forwards to FStudioBattleSystem350 with bTotal=false). `None` and `Invalid` return false, so `None` slots are inert on every tick. Any pending `FirstAttack` slot is force-failed by `FailFirstAttackTasks` when the attacker team is not 0 (team A/Playable). Units follow the selected log value: hit/finish/combo entries are counts, HitPoint is raw HP, HitPointRate is 0..1, TimeLimit is elapsed seconds, MovedDistance is metres, and CursedEnergy_Level is aggregated by maximum rather than by sum.

TargetType.simple: Who the game watches for that objective, the player, their allies, or the rival team.
TargetType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogTargetType>, default empty. Read at the same index as ValueType, PassiveType, Value and ConditionType. `Ally` collects the focused player's team characters, `Myself` only the player's character index, and `Enemy` the rival team; `None`/`Invalid` produces no character list, so EvaluateLog returns false. Evaluation uses the per-round log blocks (bTotal=false) and returns false when the player pointer is invalid or no characters resolve.

PassiveType.simple: Whether the game counts what the chosen fighter deals out or what they receive.
PassiveType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogPassiveType>, default empty. Passed at the same index to EvaluateLog. Only `Receive` selects a character's `ReceiveValues` map; `Send`, `None` and `Invalid` all select `SendValues`, so `None` is not itself a skip. The selected entries are summed over resolved characters, except `CursedEnergy_Level` (maximum) and `HitPointRate` (mean). In the export, 77 rows pair a slot-0 `ForceGauge` condition with `Receive`; hit/combo finishers are mostly `Send`, although `Attack_Hit` and `CursedEnergyAttack_Finish` use `Receive`.

Value.simple: The goal for each objective, like a hit count or Cursed Energy amount. Bigger numbers change how much must happen before the objective finishes or fails.
Value.technical: TArray<float>, default empty. `Value[i]` is copied to `FStudioMissionTaskProgress.Target`. Success conditions set `Current` to the evaluated log value and clamp it to the target when satisfied; `Failure_GreaterThanEquals` uses `max(ceil(Target-Value), 0)` and `Failure_LessThanEquals` uses `max(Value-Target, 0)`, and both fail when that value reaches zero. The HUD reset passes the authored `Value[i]` as the detail text's `VALUE` parameter, while live progress text formats runtime `Current`/`Target` as `VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE` (cast to int at reset, float thereafter). Story objective text uses `Value[i-1]` for objective index >0, and the interval wave-info widget uses `Value[0]` only. Exported thresholds are in the selected log value's units and range from 0 to 300.

ConditionType.simple: Decides whether reaching the goal completes the objective or triggers a failure. Winning the fight clears failure objectives still pending.
ConditionType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogConditionType>, default empty. Read at the same index in `Tick` and `OnEvent13`. `Success_GreaterThanEquals`/`Success_LessThanEquals` set State=1 when the evaluated value crosses `Value[i]`; `Failure_GreaterThanEquals`/`Failure_LessThanEquals` set State=-1 when their computed `Current` reaches zero. `None`/`Invalid` leave the condition pending. Pending failure conditions are converted to successes only by event 13 when `BattleResult == Win_TeamA`. Success notifications increment `CompletedCount`, call `OnPvETaskCleared(1)` and play the HUD success animation; failures play only the HUD failure animation. The export uses only `Success_GreaterThanEquals` and `Failure_GreaterThanEquals`; slot 2 in every row is `None`.

Id_BattleText_TaskDetail.simple: The battle message shown for each objective. A blank message hides it, and story tasks follow the general mission goal.
Id_BattleText_TaskDetail.technical: TArray<FName>, default empty. The battle mission-task list loops over this array (capped by the number of child task widgets) and uses the same index for `Value[i]` and `TaskProgress[i]`; `None` hides that widget. This array, not ValueType.Num(), therefore controls how many HUD slots are considered. Story objective helpers require objective index >0, validate `Index-1` in this array and reject None; index 0 is a generic mission-clear objective that does not read the row. The story reward helper applies the same `Index-1` gate. Completed story progress is persisted by task index into `FGameUserStoryMissionInfo::TaskFlags`, not by this FName.

ExcludeBindingVowsEffectType.simple: Binding Vows removed from between-fight choices in solo or tag play. Choosing more effects removes more Vows from those choices.
ExcludeBindingVowsEffectType.technical: TArray<EGameBindingVowsEffectType>, default empty. This is not part of the condition-indexed evaluation. During interval-PvE setup, each candidate vow's effect rows are collected and the candidate is removed if any `EffectType` is contained in this array; `MissionOrder.ExcludeBindingVowsEffectType` is applied to the same candidate list before the task exclusions. `None` never matches an effect. Unlike the three-slot condition arrays, all 151 exported rows carry exactly eight slots here (1184 `None` entries), with 20 rows containing real exclusions; the C++ default is an empty array and the enum defines `Invalid = 255` as its out-of-range sentinel.

notes: The catalog and export contain one MissionTaskDataTable variant with 151 unique rows. Every row has three entries in ValueType, TargetType, PassiveType, Value, ConditionType and Id_BattleText_TaskDetail: slot 0 is active in all 151, slot 1 is active in 86, and slot 2 is None in all 151; ExcludeBindingVowsEffectType always has eight entries.

Array precedence differs by consumer: runtime condition evaluation and FirstAttack/failure completion use ValueType.Num(); the HUD iterates Id_BattleText_TaskDetail.Num() and the child widget count; story objective/reward indices n>0 map to array index n-1; the interval wave-info widget uses index 0 only. The condition arrays are not length-checked against each other, and the HUD/story text paths read Value[i] after validating only the text-id index, so hand-authored rows must keep them aligned. No exported row is malformed.

Sentinels: FName `None` hides a HUD task and marks a story objective absent; ValueType `None`/`Invalid` and TargetType `None`/`Invalid` make EvaluateLog return false; PassiveType `None` still reads the Send map; ConditionType `None`/`Invalid` leave State=0. FStudioMissionTaskProgress starts at {Current=0, Target=0, State=0}, uses State 1 for success and -1 for failure, and is cleared by OnPrepareBattle (CompletedCount resets only when RetryCount<=0). A non-player (non-zero) attacker team fails pending FirstAttack tasks, and pending failure comparisons become successes only on Win_TeamA.

Success changes feed back into progression: CompletedCount is copied to ResultSnapshot.Value438, PvE reward calculations compare it with MissionTaskIds.Num(), and on a story win each TaskProgress entry with State>0 sets the matching valid TaskFlags index to 1.

Lookup chain: the manager resolves ids from MissionWave.Id_MissionTaskLottery through a weighted pick (Arcade, Story and PvE) or, for story demos, lottery element 0; 150 of 151 exported task ids are referenced by MissionTaskLotteryDataTable, with PVE_TASK_010 unreferenced in the available exports. The picked row is selected by RetryCount from the Tasks array and cached as FStudioBattleMissionTaskSystem::MissionTask, exposed via AGameBattleManager::GetMissionTask; progress is exposed via GetMissionTaskProgress.

All 25 distinct BTL_MISSION_TASK_MESSAGE_* ids used by the rows exist in every one of the 11 BattleTextDataTable locale shards, and BTL_MISSION_TASK_LABEL_0001 (the progress label) exists in all of them too.

Core task evaluation (0x1055FE0, 0x105F400), HUD reset (0x14E09F0), demo objective helpers (0x1310B70, 0x130A4B0) and lottery pick (0x1302490) are recorded as byte-matched in status/functions.json. Setup paths such as 0x13A1E40/0x13A3B70/0x13A70D0 and interval vow filtering 0x1303F60 are only behavioural, and HUD progress formatter 0x14F8310 carries a HOLD verdict; no retail Blueprint graphs or live game capture were available, so widget bindings and any BP/data-asset wiring remain unverified.

usages.detail: Loads MissionTaskDataTable via its named primary-asset loader into `MissionTaskDataTables` at DTM+0x9E0; all row lookups walk that table array.

BattleArcade_PickLotteryTask removes None task ids from MissionTaskLottery.Id_MissionTask, sums Weights, and makes a weighted FRand pick; the chosen id is resolved against MissionTaskDataTables at line 158 with null kept.

GamePvE_MakeMissionTasks fills `FGamePvESettings::MissionTaskIds` one-per-wave from the same lottery picker; PvE Solo/Tag later resolve those ids at GamePhase_BattlePvESolo.cpp:494 and GamePhase_BattlePvETag.cpp:69.
Story battle setup resolves lottery-picked task rows, hands them to SetupStoryMission, and at line 417 copies successful TaskProgress indices into the user's story TaskFlags.

Tick evaluates each ValueType-indexed condition through EvaluateLog with bTotal=false, creates/updates the index-keyed TaskProgress entry, and notifies HUD/counters; FailFirstAttackTasks (line 631) and OnEvent13 (line 733) mutate the same cache.
Aliases the cached current row and its progress map as GetMissionTask / GetMissionTaskProgress for the HUD and phase code.
HUD reset uses the current row's Id_BattleText_TaskDetail and Value for each child widget, overlays State/Current/Target from the cache, hides None rows, and ticks live progress from the same cache.

Story_GetDemoMissionTask walks StoryDemo -> StoryMission -> StoryMissionWave -> MissionWave -> lottery element 0; the helpers at lines 580-619 use TextDetail[Index-1] for objective presence/completion/text and line 1238 gates reward items on the same shifted id.
IntervalPvE_PickBindingVows filters candidate binding vows using MissionOrder exclusions first (line 650) and then each selected task row's ExcludeBindingVowsEffectType (line 665).
Displays only element 0 of Id_BattleText_TaskDetail and Value as the interval wave's task line, requiring both arrays to be non-empty and the text id non-None.
OnPvETaskCleared increments PvE solo/tag task-clear user records for each notified success, feeding the task-clear achievements.
